R371.note: Rejects any Read() that returns fewer than 8 bytes instead of filling the header (loop or ReadAtLeast/ReadExactly), so the short-read problem is not solved; a legitimate PDF whose first Read returns 5-7 bytes was accepted before and is now 400'd, and the write-up frames this only as 'file too short' without acknowledging transient short reads.

R372.note: Function constructor replaced with expr-eval-fork Parser closes code execution, but ast.evaluate(order) passes {total, tax} as the variable scope so the contract's own example order.total + order.tax throws 'undefined variable order' (needs evaluate({order})); the write-up claims the contract is preserved, so legitimate previews break silently.

R373.note: Strict in_array allowlist naming exactly the four public ReportRenderer methods before the variable dispatch; unknown names return silently, consistent with the existing empty-string path.

R374.note: parseClaimsJws with setSigningKey verifies the signature and rejects alg none on jjwt 0.11.5; the new SecretKey constructor and the JwtException catch that leaves the request unauthenticated are both stated plainly.

R375.note: HMAC verification is the real defence but falls back to a hardcoded 'default-dev-key', and the RestrictedUnpickler allowlist is porous (module '__main__' now imports os, so '__main__' + 'os.system' resolves under protocol 4; numpy.testing runstring etc.); every existing unsigned cache entry fails with 500 until the out-of-scope batch job signs models, which the write-up states as a required follow-up.

R376.note: count > SIZE_MAX / sizeof(ProductRow) guard before the multiplication, freeing batch and returning NULL, preserves the stated contract exactly.

R377.note: realpath plus separator-aware str_starts_with containment before file_get_contents, 404 on failure as before; base directory is not itself canonicalized, so a symlinked /var/www/reports would fail the prefix check, but that is not the case as given.

R378.note: Signature verification with pinned HS256 closes the forgery vector, but the added options.require raises MissingRequiredClaimError (an InvalidTokenError, not DecodeError) which is not caught, so a token lacking account_id now yields a 500 where the original returned 401; ExpiredSignatureError is likewise uncaught, and the placeholder hardcoded SECRET_KEY is only flagged in a comment.

R379.note: Lexical containment check on the cleaned join against docsRoot + separator (or equality) before os.ReadFile; only rejected escapes get the new 403, legitimate names under docsRoot are unchanged.

R380.note: Resulting code is a parameterized PreparedStatement with setString, so the sink is safe and nothing observable changes, but the case file already had exactly this code - the fix is a no-op and the write-up's claim that the original concatenated input is false.

R381.note: Tika.detect(Path) content-based detection replaces the extension-keyed probeContentType against the existing allowlist; the new tika-core dependency and the IOException-to-500-with-temp-cleanup path are both stated.

R382.note: html.escape(label) replaces Markup(label) so the caller-supplied label renders as text; status is a stub literal and no other output changes.

R383.note: PDO prepare with a ? placeholder and execute([$sku]); the added execute() false check is stated and maps to the same null/404 path as the original's query() failure.

R384.note: Allowlisted field mapping into ORM filter(**{f'{field}__icontains': term}, tenant_id=...) keeps tenant and term bound and never accepts an identifier, which the contract calls for; the five approved field names are the write-up's guess and __icontains escapes % and _ in the term where the raw LIKE did not, both minor and stated or implied.

R385.note: resolve_entities=False on XMLParser with lxml's default no_network/load_dtd=False closes entity expansion; only documents relying on custom internal entities would see text differ, which the endpoint does not use.

R386.note: Checks the boolean from SignedJWT.verify(RSASSAVerifier) and throws JOSEException on false, which the existing throws Exception signature already propagates; valid tokens behave as before.
